newsitem.title: USA: Japan, U.S. to cooperate on currencies, debt relief.
newsitem.headline: Japan, U.S. to cooperate on currencies, debt relief.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin agreed on Saturday to maintain close cooperation in managing their currencies, a Japanese Finance Ministry official said.
They also agreed to work closely in strengthening the international financial system and providing debt relief for poorer nations, the official told reporters.
Kubo and Rubin met during the annual International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings in Washington.
The Japanese official said Rubin did not ask Japan to take further fiscal steps to stimulate its domestic economy.
Kubo told Rubin he had read an article about Rubin saying it was critically important that Japan continue to pursue a policy aimed at promoting domestic demand-led growth, the official said.
Kubo also told Rubin that he would keep close watch over Japan's economic movement and work toward economic recovery based on domestic demand.
However, Kubo also mentioned the importance of rebuilding state finances, and Rubin acknowledged Kubo's emphasis on the need for fiscal consolidation, the official said.
Kubo and Rubin also agreed to work toward reaching an agreement on a dispute over insurance.
Asked whether the United States made any mention of sanctions, the official said there was no such discussion.
"They agreed that it was particularly important that the two reach an agreement as quickly as possible, and they also agreed to be flexible in tackling it," the official said.
The two agreed to coordinate in coping with various risks in the international finance system and study such issues as electronic money.
Rubin and Kubo conferred before a meeting of top financial officials from the Group of Seven leading industrial nations -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
They did not go into detail on what types of debt relief for poorer nations Japan and the United States would cooperate on, the Japanese official said.
Rich industrial countries are considering increasing the amount of help they are prepared to offer debt-ridden nations under a multibillion-dollar international initiative.
